name: Wathawurrung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read Blake, Clark & Krishna-Pillay 1998, Wathawurrung: The Language of the Geelong-Ballarat Area (PL C-147, ANU open repository full text): 19th-century-source reconstruction, no word-stress statement anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 1998. Classifying Victorian languages. In B. J. Blake (ed.), Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria (PL C-147), 1-58. (same volume)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.5 and p.13 fn.11: 'Although in most Australian languages the stress is on the first syllable, in Madi-Madi.. the stress was on the second syllable in words of three or more syllables..' -- a statement about Madhi-Madhi (Hercus 1986), nothing specific to Wathawurrung.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1904. Language of the Wuddyawurru tribe, Victoria. Zeitschrift fur Ethnologie 36: 729-734 (orthography deferred to his Kogai article, same vol., pp.28-30).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grammar notes and c.150-word vocabulary from Mathews' own fieldwork; the orthography section (Kogai article) marks vowel length and consonant values only; no accent/stress statement.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1902. The Aboriginal languages of Victoria. Journal and Proceedings of the Royal Society of New South Wales 36: 71-106 ('Orthography' p.76; 'Tyapwurru and Wuddyawurru dialects' pp.84-86).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Orthography section gives letter values and vowel-length marking only; Wuddyawurru section is a pronoun paradigm; no accent/stress statement.

sources.citation: WALS Online CLDF (held by the project: language wth Wathawurrung.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only feature 116A coded (source Blake et al. 1998); no stress features (14A-17A).

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J., Ian D. Clark & Sharnthi H. Krishna-Pillay. 1998. Wathawurrung: the language of the Geelong-Ballarat area. In B. J. Blake (ed.), Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria (Pacific Linguistics C-147), 59-154. Canberra: ANU. (whole volume downloaded via DOI 10.15144/PL-C147 -> sealang PL archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage)); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: Sec. 2 Phonology (pp.66-70: phoneme inventory reconstructed from 19th-c. spellings, vowels, phonotactics) contains no statement on word stress/accent. Only indirect hint p.59: the second vowel of the ethnonym Wathawurrung 'is possibly u, but heard as an unstressed schwa'. 'Stressed/unstressed pronouns' in sec. 3 refer to free vs enclitic pronoun sets, not word prosody.

sources.citation: Cary, John J. 1898. Vocabularies of the Geelong and Colac tribes, collected in 1840 [from the MSS of Francis Tuckfield]. Report of the 7th meeting of the Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science 7: 840-872.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Letters' and 'Sounds' (pp.847-848): Tuckfield's marked vowels are long/short values; 'Emphasis is sometimes marked by reduplicating a word, or adding a syllable' is pragmatic emphasis, not word stress. No accent statement.

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. c.1900-1904. Manuscript notebooks and field notes on Wuddyawurru (from 'Mrs Richards, Yarrar' and Jack Phillips), R. H. Mathews papers, National Library of Australia MS 8006 (folder/documents BE, AY as cited by Blake et al. 1998:65).

sources.note: Only first-hand notes taken from the last speakers by a trained (if amateur) recorder; if any accent marks exist for this language they would be here. Low expectation: his published orthography never marks accent.
